endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: Should the Safeguard LLM classify a query as inappropriate — particularly those seeking medical recommendations like differential diagnoses or treatment plans, which are beyond the system's capabilities — it will issue a rejection notice.

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
endorsements.issuer: National Institute of Standards and Technology
endorsements.quote: Leverage feedback and recommendations from organizational boards or committees related to the deployment of GAI applications and content provenance when using third-party pre-trained models.

endorsements.title: A Prompt Engineering Framework for Large Language Model-Based Mental Health Chatbots: Conceptual Framework
endorsements.quote: If the LLM’s output is flagged, the system may attempt to regenerate the response with an updated prompt or revert to a safe, predefined template.

endorsements.title: Conversational AI for perinatal mental health: promise, limits, and a human-AI stepped-care framework
endorsements.quote: Digital doulas must incorporate similar non-negotiable deterministic overrides.

endorsements.title: Ethical Considerations in Personal Health Large Language Models
endorsements.quote: PH-LLMs should incorporate a sequential safety pipeline that combines input filtering, retrieval-augmented generation from curated authoritative sources, output checking against structured medical knowledge resources, and uncertainty signaling where technically feasible [ 85 , 116 - 118 ].

endorsements.title: Generative AI for pre-consultation mental health triage in disorders of gut-brain interaction
endorsements.quote: Fourth, escalation-sensitive content—suicidal ideation, self-harm, severe nutritional risk—should bypass the generative synthesis step entirely and follow deterministic, rule-based routing, as LLM-generated paraphrases of safety-critical disclosures introduce unacceptable risk.

endorsements.title: Engineering safety into AI-assisted music medicine for headache management: a transparent guardrail framework
endorsements.quote: It intercepts any output that violates predefined criteria, such as a maximum allowable tempo (< 100 BPM), sudden transient decibel spikes, high-frequency spectral power concentrations, or syncopated percussive patterns.

evidence.title: Community Learning Ledgers for Cancer Navigation in Small Island Developing States
evidence.outcome: Rejection of adversarial probes by governance contract
evidence.effect: Governance contract rejected every adversarial probe even as off-codebook queries rose from 2.4% to 26.7%
evidence.quote: After active clinical promotion ceased, off-codebook queries rose from 2.4% to 26.7% across phases while the governance contract continued to reject every adversarial probe — the community persisted but drifted from the cancer codebook absent clinician curation.
evidence.sample_unit: patient screening queries (plus 207 community sessions descriptively classified)
evidence.country: Caribbean (ten jurisdictions, led by Trinidad and Tobago)

evidence.title: ETHOS: Towards a Modular Ethics Framework for Clinical Multi-Agent Systems
evidence.outcome: Decision reliability of hepatology multi-agent system with runtime ethics oversight suppressing or revising failing outputs
evidence.effect: ETHOS improved decision reliability by detecting incomplete, inconsistent, or out-of-scope evidence and increasing abstention when safe recommendations could not be supported; no numbers in abstract.
evidence.quote: Results show that ETHOS improves decision reliability by detecting incomplete, inconsistent, or out-of-scope evidence and appropriately increasing abstention when safe recommendations cannot be supported.

evidence.title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Colonoscopy Preparation Assistance: Correctness and Diversity in Synthetic Dialogues
evidence.outcome: Error and harmful response rates after automated safety filter replacing incorrect responses with deferral message
evidence.effect: Applying an automated safety filter reduced overall error rates but failed to eliminate harmful responses.
evidence.quote: Applying an automated safety filter reduced overall error rates but failed to eliminate harmful responses.
evidence.sample_unit: synthetic patient-AI Coach dialogues (250 per model x 5 models)

evidence.title: A Novel Cognitive Behavioral Therapy-Based Generative AI Tool (Socrates 2.0) to Facilitate Socratic Dialogue: Protocol for a Mixed Methods Feasibility Study
evidence.outcome: Harmful responses in simulated scenarios and whether the AI supervisor corrected them
evidence.effect: In about 500 scenarios, Socrates 2.0 gave harmful responses in under 1% of cases, and the AI supervisor promptly corrected the dialogue each time.
evidence.quote: Moreover, tests in approximately 500 scenarios showed that Socrates 2.0 engaged in harmful responses in under 1% of cases, with the AI supervisor promptly correcting the dialogue each time.
evidence.sample_unit: participants (planned 100 users and 50 clinicians; 55 recruited so far)

evidence.title: Preventing Another Tessa: Modular Safety Middleware For Health-Adjacent AI Assistants
evidence.outcome: Interception of unsafe prompts by lexical gate plus in-line LLM policy filter, cost and latency
evidence.effect: Hybrid middleware achieved perfect interception of unsafe prompts at baseline cost and latency, outperforming traditional multi-stage pipelines (synthetic evaluations; sample size not reported in text).
evidence.quote: Using synthetic evaluations, we show that this design achieves perfect interception of unsafe prompts at baseline cost and latency, outperforming traditional multi-stage pipelines.

evidence.title: MindGuard: Guardrail Classifiers for Multi-Turn Mental Health Support
evidence.outcome: Attack success and harmful engagement rates in adversarial multi-turn interactions with classifier safeguard
evidence.effect: Paired with clinician language models, MindGuard yields lower attack success and harmful engagement rates than general-purpose safeguards (no numbers given in the abstract).
evidence.quote: Our classifiers reduce false positives at high-recall operating points and, when paired with clinician language models, help achieve lower attack success and harmful engagement rates in adversarial multi-turn interactions compared to general-purpose safeguards.

evidence.title: Detecting Jailbreak Attempts in Clinical Training LLMs Through Automated Linguistic Feature Extraction
evidence.outcome: Jailbreak detection performance of a feature-based classifier layer on clinical simulation dialogue
evidence.effect: Strong overall performance reported across cross-validation and held-out evaluations; no numeric values in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Across cross-validation and held-out evaluations, the system achieves strong overall performance, indicating that LLM-derived linguistic features provide an effective basis for automated jailbreak detection.

evidence.title: GrandGuard: Taxonomy, Benchmark, and Safeguards for Elderly-Chatbot Interaction Safety
evidence.outcome: Unsafe-prompt detection accuracy of safeguard models for elderly-specific risks
evidence.effect: Fine-tuned Llama-Guard-3 reached up to 96.2% and policy-enhanced gpt-oss-safeguard-20b up to 90.9% unsafe-prompt detection accuracy.
evidence.quote: We mitigate these failures with two safeguards: a fine-tuned Llama-Guard-3 and a policy-enhanced gpt-oss-safeguard-20b, achieving up to 96.2% and 90.9% unsafe-prompt detection accuracy, respectively.

evidence.title: MultiTurnPSB: Evaluating Multi-Turn Jailbreak Attacks an dClassifier-Based Defenses for Medical AI Safety
evidence.outcome: Turn 4 unsafe responses with input-side classifier, and false alarm rate on benign queries
evidence.effect: The classifier reduced Turn 4 unsafe responses by 52 percentage points despite severe accuracy degradation, but produced a 45% false alarm rate on benign queries.
evidence.quote: A lightweight input-side classifier reduces Turn 4 unsafe responses by 52 percentage points despite severe accuracy degradation, but the 45% false alarm rate on benign queries is the primary deployment constraint.

evidence.title: When Medical Safety Alignment Fails: A Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs on High-Risk Medical Queries
evidence.outcome: Effect of external guardrail models on blocking unsafe high-risk medical queries and outputs
evidence.effect: External guardrails reduced some failures but introduced brittle blocking and weak safe helpfulness; no numbers in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Results reveal a substantial gap between apparent alignment and medical safety: aligned models can still produce unsafe or actionable responses, medical fine-tuning can amplify harmful specificity, and external guardrails reduce some failures while introducing brittle blocking and weak safe helpfulness.

evidence.title: ECHO: A Locally-Deployable Agentic Health Assistant with Temporal Memory, Safety Guardrails, and Speech Assessment
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and unsafe recall of a hybrid safety layer classifying and blocking unsafe health queries
evidence.effect: Signed GNN safety classifier reached 88.8% accuracy and 90.6% unsafe recall on 2,537 Turkish queries, outperforming zero-shot LLM baselines including Llama 3.3 70B.
evidence.quote: a signed graph neural network (GNN) with APPNP-style propagation classifies boundary cases by clinical intent, achieving 88.8% accuracy and 90.6% unsafe recall on a 2,537-query annotated Turkish health dataset while outperforming zero-shot LLM baselines including Llama 3.3 70B.

evidence.title: LLMs Can Do Medical Harm: Stress-Testing Clinical Decisions Under Social Pressure
evidence.outcome: Proportion of potentially harmful responses with versus without brief safety mitigation cue
evidence.effect: Mitigation cue reduced harmful decisions from 16.6% to 10.1% (p<0.001), but did not eliminate harm.
evidence.quote: Mitigation reduced harmful decisions from 16.6% to 10.1% (p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Deployment protocol and base model jointly determine residual risk in rule-based clinical LLM supervision
evidence.outcome: Deploy violation rate with rule-based sentinel blocking/escalating unsafe outputs
evidence.effect: Under handoff-on all models had deploy violation rates at most 6%; strict violation rates 1.5% to 49.5%; HealthBench Hard 0.0% deploy VR.
evidence.quote: Under handoff-on, all models achieved deploy violation rates at most 6%, though strict violation rates (counting blocked and escalated outputs) ranged from 1.5% to 49.5%, showing wide variation in how many outputs the sentinel blocks or escalates per model.

evidence.title: Development and evaluation of an agentic LLM based RAG framework for evidence-based patient education
evidence.outcome: Validation agent accuracy in blocking harmful patient education content
evidence.effect: Accuracy correlated with model size; Gemma-2-27b 0.82, Qwen2.5-32b 0.80; models <14B generally <0.50; Jais and Fanar 0.40 (blocked none); top performers failed on category 3 harmful PEMs.
evidence.quote: Models under 14B parameters generally scored below 0.50 accuracy, whereas only those with ≥27B parameters exceeded 0.80, suggesting sufficient parameter capacity is needed for reliable content validation in PE workflows.
evidence.sample_unit: patient education questions (12 LLMs x 4 setups); 50 PEMs for validation agent test

evidence.title: Beyond Simulations: What 20,000 Real Conversations Reveal About Mental Health AI Safety
evidence.outcome: Harmful content generation across suicide/NSSI, eating disorder, and substance use benchmarks
evidence.effect: Purpose-built versus general-purpose harmful-content rates: suicide/NSSI .4-11.27% vs 29.0-54.4%; eating disorder 8.4% vs 54.0%; substance use 9.9% vs 45.0%.
evidence.quote: The purpose-built AI was significantly less likely than general-purpose LLMs to produce harmful content across suicide/NSSI (.4-11.27% vs 29.0-54.4%), eating disorder (8.4% vs 54.0%), and substance use (9.9% vs 45.0%) benchmarks.

evidence.title: One Year Later...The Harms Persist, But So Do We!
evidence.outcome: Whether LLM safeguards block harmful mental health outputs across conditions and adversarial prompts
evidence.effect: Safeguards are inadequate and inconsistent across clinical conditions; failure rates reach up to 100% for several conditions.
evidence.quote: General-purpose large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for mental health-related conversations, yet safety guardrails remain inadequate and inconsistent across clinical conditions.

commentary.bottom_line: Fourteen studies test automated blocking or filtering of generative AI queries and outputs, and most report fewer unsafe outputs, but 13 are benchmarks or simulations and four found that filters missed harmful content or blocked benign queries. No study measured whether alerting humans to deviations changed patient outcomes.

perspectives.view: Of 14 studies, 13 are level 4 or 5 benchmarks or simulations. Only one, with 207 screening queries, comes from a real deployment. Four report null or mixed results, and several abstracts give no numbers. Indirect outcomes, inconsistent findings, and imprecision suggest very low certainty that the practice reduces harm to patients.

A safety filter applied to 1,250 synthetic coaching dialogues lowered error rates but did not remove harmful responses. A safety cue cut harmful decisions from 16.6% to 10.1% without eliminating them. Top models in a validation agent test failed on one category of harmful materials. These results suggest blocking layers reduce harm but leave gaps.

An input classifier cut unsafe responses by 52 percentage points but flagged 45% of benign queries. External guardrails produced brittle blocking and weak safe helpfulness. A hybrid middleware reported full interception at baseline cost and latency, but only on synthetic tests. False rejections at these rates may lead clinicians and patients to work around the tool.

No study measured the staffing cost of human alerts. A rule-based sentinel with handoff kept deploy violation rates at or below 6%, while strict violation rates ranged from 1.5% to 49.5%. A 45% false alarm rate on benign queries would generate review volume that may exceed what staff can absorb.

Two benchmarks used non-English content. A classifier reached 88.8% accuracy and 90.6% unsafe recall on 2,537 Turkish health queries. In a Qatar study, the Jais and Fanar models scored 0.40 and blocked no harmful materials. An older-adult benchmark reported up to 96.2% detection. Performance appears to vary by language and model.

In about 500 simulated scenarios, an AI supervisor corrected each harmful chatbot response, but the correction came from software rather than a person. No study reported how patients experienced rejection notices or whether they reached a human after a block. Frequent refusals of benign questions may erode patient trust.

commentary.research_gap: No study tested the full practice in live clinical use, with rejection notices paired with human alerts. None measured patient harm, false rejection burden, staff response time, or patient access to a human after a block. Prospective deployment studies that report these outcomes with numbers would address the gap.
commentary.underserved_note: Two benchmarks tested non-English health content, one with Turkish queries and one with patient education materials in Qatar. The one real deployment ran in Caribbean jurisdictions. No study included Medicaid, safety-net, or low-literacy populations. Health systems serving those populations cannot assume that the reported detection and false alarm rates apply to their patients' queries.
